assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials: a clear theoretical prediction of flat bands at a specific twist angle, followed by experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. It is a discovery with a precise, falsifiable origin and enormous downstream impact across condensed matter. From a materials-and-interfaces viewpoint, the control of atomic registry at the interface is the heart of the discovery.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is the decisive prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive 2018 experiments. This supports a clean theory-plus-experiment split of three. Other experimental groups (for example in the correlated-insulator work) and other theorists of twisted graphene could be argued, and I cannot independently verify the full priority record.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups worldwide over several years, with the interpretation of superconductivity still debated in detail but the existence of flat bands and correlated phases secure. Recognition now is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Mechanism of the superconductivity is still contested, so the prize would need to rest on the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated states rather than on the mechanism.
Credit for the experimental side is concentrated on one group while related early work on twisted graphene exists; allocation is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made superconducting artificial atoms coupled to microwave resonators a controllable quantum platform, enabling dispersive readout, strong coupling and the architecture of present superconducting quantum processors. It is original, clear and has lasting impact on both fundamental quantum optics and technology. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, so this is a natural but distinct successor topic.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf (with Girvin) are the central figures: the 2004 proposal and first strong-coupling demonstration. Only three can be chosen from four credited names; Girvin's co-authorship of the proposal makes the choice between him and Blais difficult. I select the proposal-and-demonstration trio with the experimental weight in mind, while acknowledging the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over two decades by independent groups and widely deployed; recognition is mature, though proximity to the 2025 prize may weigh on timing.
uncertainties: Four credited names but at most three laureates; the exclusion of Girvin or Blais is an unresolved allocation question.
Overlap with the topic of the most recent prize could be seen as too close.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock is an invention with a clear concept (magic wavelength trapping of many atoms) and demonstrated order-of-magnitude gains in precision, redefining the frontier of timekeeping and enabling tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It fits the criterion of a discovery or invention with concrete, verifiable performance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye's group realised and drove the clocks to record performance. Two laureates give a fair, compact configuration, though other groups contributed to strontium and ytterbium clocks and I cannot verify every priority detail.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by multiple national laboratories and ongoing progress toward a redefinition of the second; timely and mature, though the redefinition itself is still pending.
uncertainties: Contributions of other clock groups (for example ytterbium lattice clocks) and the relationship to earlier ion-clock and frequency-comb recognition are not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions: the observation of a skyrmion lattice in MnSi by neutron scattering and real-space Lorentz transmission electron microscopy imaging in thin films, together with the emergent electrodynamics (topological Hall effect, spin-transfer at ultralow current). The discovery is clear and conceptually original; real-space imaging by TEM is central to its credibility, which I regard as a particularly persuasive form of evidence.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer's group provided the bulk discovery, Tokura's group the real-space imaging and room-temperature materials, and Rosch the theory of emergent electromagnetism and current-driven motion. This is a plausible three-way split. Other contributors (for example Bogdanov for the theoretical prediction, and the Lorentz-TEM imaging authors) are not in the supplied credit list, which limits fairness.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many materials and techniques; the physics is stable. Technological promise (racetrack memory) remains unrealised, so the prize would rest on the discovery.
uncertainties: Theoretical predecessors outside the credited names complicate attribution.
Application relevance is overstated in some literature and should not be counted as evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond turned a defect into a room-temperature quantum sensor and spin qubit, with applications from nanoscale magnetometry to biological sensing. A defect-in-a-solid system where structure and spectroscopy are decisive appeals to me as a microscopist.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single-centre optical detection and coherent control; Lukin's group extended this to quantum registers and sensing. Gruber and others are not in the credit list. The trio is defensible but the sensing contributions are broadly distributed.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and now a mature field with many groups; the foundational demonstrations date from 1997 onwards, so recognition would be timely or somewhat late.
uncertainties: Broad community contributions to NV sensing make the choice of three laureates somewhat arbitrary.
Separation between the single-defect discovery and the later sensing applications is not fully clear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect: a theoretical prediction followed by experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, creating a new classification of electronic phases. The importance and originality are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theoretical proposal, and Molenkamp's group the first experimental realisation in HgTe wells. Theoretical work by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang on HgTe, and the three-dimensional generalisations, are outside the credit list, so the configuration leaves out important contributors; I cannot resolve this within the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by many groups and materials. The field is mature, and recognition would arguably not be premature, though attribution questions remain.
uncertainties: Absence of Zhang (deceased) and of the HgTe prediction authors from the credit set raises fairness concerns.
The 2016 prize already recognised topological phases, so overlap needs to be weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the observation of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and later quantum gas microscopy, provides a controllable platform for strongly correlated problems. Its impact on both atomic physics and many-body theory is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and Cirac) supplied the theoretical proposals; Bloch and Greiner carried out the decisive experiments, including the Mott transition and single-site imaging. The credited list has five names, so choosing three requires leaving out important contributors such as Cirac and Dalibard.
assessment.maturity: The platform is well established and widely replicated; the topic is mature, but it overlaps with earlier cold-atom prizes and the quantum simulation payoff is still developing.
uncertainties: Five credited names for at most three places; allocation among theorists and experimentalists is unresolved.
Overlap with earlier ultracold atom recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Titanium-sapphire gain media and passive mode-locking made practical, tunable femtosecond lasers possible and underpin much of ultrafast science, including the attosecond techniques the committee recognised in 2023. This is an enabling invention with enormous reach, though its importance is partly through the applications it supports.
assessment.attribution: Moulton developed the Ti:sapphire laser, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking, and Keller introduced semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) mode-locking. The supplied credit supports a three-way split, but the relative weight of Kerr-lens versus SESAM contributions is a question I cannot settle, and Spence and others are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly mature, in universal use for decades; recognition is arguably late rather than premature, and the committee has previously honoured closely related laser and ultrafast work.
uncertainties: Proximity to previous recognition of chirped pulse amplification and attosecond pulses.
Unclear priority between Kerr-lens and saturable absorber mode-locking.
